title: A crowd from one cycle
summary: Turn one hopping cycle into a crowd with Repeat in a Line or Grid, then put them out of step with Stagger.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text: Hopper is a graphic symbol with a 12-frame hop that loops. In this lesson one instance of it becomes a whole crowd, with no copying and pasting.

steps.title: Select the hopper
steps.text: Press V for the Selection tool and click the hopper on the stage.

steps.title: Open the Behaviors panel
steps.text: Choose Window > Behaviors if it is not showing. It lists what is on the selection and the settings of each.

steps.title: Make a grid of copies
steps.text: Click Add Behavior and choose Repeat in a Line or Grid. Five copies stand in a row.

steps.title: More rows
steps.text: Set Copies across to 12 and Rows to 5, and Space across to 90 and Space down to 80: a crowd of sixty.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. All sixty hop together, like a drill team.

steps.title: Put them out of step
steps.text:
Add Stagger. Each copy now runs its loop a few frames after the one before.

Tick In random order for a crowd that hops each to its own time.

steps.title: Shake up the rows
steps.text: Add Wiggle too, with a small amount, so no two stand in quite the same place. Each copy wiggles on its own.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
One cycle made a crowd. The same works for grass, rain, a stadium or a field of flowers: any graphic with a loop.

Effector changes copies by where they are, for a wave through the crowd; try it next.
